chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not offer a sacrifice with the one who limps, its limp being evident, nor with the lean one, nor with the scabby one, nor with the one with torn ears, nor with the one with the tail cut off, nor with the one that has no eye.'

key_terms.حَذَّاءُ: A one with the tail cut off
key_terms.عَضْبَاءُ: A one without an eye (blind in one eye)

ai.seo_question: What physical defects disqualify an animal from sacrifice in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details six specific physical defects ('ayb) that disqualify sacrificial animals, reflecting the Shia emphasis on selecting the best and most sound livestock for worship. These criteria ensure the sacrifice is free from obvious imperfections, aligning with the Prophetic tradition of offering the 'khalas' (pure/clean) animal. The ruling underscores the spiritual integrity of the act by linking physical wholeness to ritual acceptability.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father, from his<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not offer a sacrifice with the one who limps between its walk, nor with the lean one, nor with the scabby, nor with the clumsy, nor with the torn ears, nor with the tail cut off’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has narrated from his ancestors who have stated this Hadith.

‘The Holy prophet, O Allah, grant compensation, to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “You must not sacrifice as offering what (of animal) is limping that is apparent, an emaciated, scabby, with torn ears or cut-off tail.’””
